newsitem.title: USA: ARCO wins approval for North Sea gas project.
newsitem.headline: ARCO wins approval for North Sea gas project.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co said Thursday its ARCO British Limited unit and partners received approval from the British government to develope two natural gas and condensate projects in the Central North Sea.
The combined projects are estimated to contain just under 100 million barrels of recoverable oil equivalent, net to ARCO.

One project, Shearwater field, is due to come onstream in 2000, and will generate 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of natural gas and 80,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of condensate when producing at capacity, the company said.
A second project, the Elgin/Franklin fields, also due on-stream in April 2000, will generate 500 mmcfd of natural gas and 160,000 bpd of condensate at capacity.
ARCO holds a 27.5 percent interest in the Shearwater project, which will be operated by Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell U.K. Exploration and Production.
It holds a 1.76 percent interest in the Elgin/Franklin fields, operated by Elf Aquitaine's Elf U.K., plc.
Discovered in 1991, Shearwater is a high pressure, high temperature field located 125 miles east of Aberdeen, Scotland in about 300 feet of water.
Gas from the field will be exported to the Bacton terminal via a $600 million, 300-mile pipeline named the Shearwater Elgin Area Line (SEAL).

The SEAL pipeline will be jointly owned by the Shearwater partners and partners in the Elgin/Franklin fields. Liquids from all the fields will be sent via a spur line into the existing Forties Pipeline System.
